root_idea.summary: The root centers on holding or clamping something with the teeth, especially biting.
root_idea.development: From physical biting, the lexical field extends to gripping or clinging, repeated pressure, severity and distress, tenacity, experienced strength, and several names for fodder or coarse vegetation.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect-tense citation form عَضَّ.

senses.usage_conditions: The basic physical action of gripping or clamping something with the teeth. Intensified or repeated biting is expressed by related derived forms, without constituting a separate Quranic sense.

senses.definition: To bite one’s hands, fingers, or fingertips as an expression of intense anger, hatred, remorse, or regret.
senses.usage_conditions: A conventional body-part construction: the Quranic usage at 3:119 conveys rage and hostility, while 25:27 conveys regret. The cited body-part object does not restrict the ordinary lexical verb to that object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cling to, hold fast to, or adhere closely to a person, property, knowledge, a course, or a matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of gripping with the teeth; it may describe steadfast attachment or close management.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bite one’s tongue, conventionally as an expression of restraint or forbearance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The tongue-biting proverb is a conventional figurative use distinct from the Quranic hand-biting construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To defame, speak evil of, or backbite someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use, sometimes expressed as biting with the tongue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To grip, pinch, press, or hurt as though by biting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied figuratively to an instrument gripping a spear, a saddle hurting its bearer, or weapons wounding people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become severe, hard, distressing, or afflictive; also, in some descriptions, to become strong or hard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to affairs, war, time, fortune, and occasionally a person or thing described as becoming strong.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone experienced or expert through travel or the management of affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use in which difficult experience is said to bite or work upon a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To jest or play amorously with a young woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form II usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw water from a difficult or deep well of the type called عَضُوضٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form II construction referring to arduous water-drawing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed camels with the fodder called عُضّ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form II agricultural or pastoral use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bite one another or bite each other.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form III construction, especially of beasts or two parties.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To grapple with or struggle against a difficult life.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative reciprocal construction describing sustained hardship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone bite or seize something with the teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form IV construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To tell someone abusively to bite a specified obscene object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported abusive imperative formula, preserved as a specialized idiomatic use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a sword wound someone or make an instrument cleave to and grip a body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative causative Form IV use applied to swords and cupping instruments.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a well, to become difficult or arduous to draw from.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV construction connected with the quality عَضُوضٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For camels to feed on عُضّ or عِضّ; of land, to abound in such fodder or trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV pastoral and environmental use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fodder or feed for livestock, including crushed date-stones, grain, dough, trefoil, and dry herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The exact fodder material varies by authority and regional usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Coarse trees, shrubs, thick firewood, or other rough woody vegetation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical or fuel sense, distinct from the fodder sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lock that scarcely opens or will not open.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative nominal use based on tenacious closure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who keeps close to, manages, and rigorously attends to property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person characterized by close control of possessions or livelihood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Niggardly, tenacious, or avaricious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative characterization associated with holding tightly to property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Evil in disposition; bad, wicked, or malignant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival character description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A strong or forceful man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive personal description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person having sufficient strength or power for travel or fighting, and thereby experienced in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in compounds such as “strong for travel” or “strong for fighting.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: An equal, match, opponent, or adversary.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational noun applied to one person in relation to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cunning, intelligent, skilful, knowledgeable, eloquent, or contentious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The range includes a person able to understand obscure matters or outwit others.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Small thorny trees or shrubs, including kinds of acacia and related growth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical term whose exact species list varies among authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bite.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ordinary deverbal noun for one biting act or bite-mark.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Something available to be bitten and eaten; edible food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions for having or tasting nothing to eat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Trees or plants that have become thick, coarse, dry, tough, or hard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical description of mature or hardened growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act or fault of an animal, especially a beast or horse, that bites people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A recognized defect in an animal offered for sale.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Endurance of distress or affliction with patience.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression عِضَاضُ عَيْشٍ for enduring a harsh life.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse or camel that bites, especially one habitually or repeatedly biting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive animal adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bow whose string clings or sticks to its handle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a bow’s fit or action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman whose vaginal opening is so narrow that penetration is difficult or impossible.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare anatomical usage reported in the lexical tradition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A deep, narrow, or otherwise difficult well or water source from which drawing water is arduous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can also describe the distress caused to the water-drawer; some reports associate it with abundant water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Severe, grievous, distressing, or afflictive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to time, fortune, or war.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unjust or tyrannical rule or dominion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive figurative epithet for rule that oppresses its subjects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A calamity or misfortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative nominal use derived from the notion of something biting or afflicting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An associate, companion, or equal in age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational description of one person in relation to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel that feeds on trees of the type called عِضّ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized active-participial animal description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of sweet, very sweet black date from Hejer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regional fruit name; the feminine form names an individual date or its tree.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or thing in which or on which one can lay hold; a foothold or means of settlement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used literally of a place and figuratively of something that provides a grasp or support in an affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person whose camels feed on عِضّ or related trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized active-participial pastoral description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land abounding in the trees or vegetation called عِضّ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized environmental adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An ass bitten repeatedly and lacerated by other asses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial description of an animal subjected to repeated biting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bitten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The passive participle of the basic Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The tip or projecting end of the nose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare and explicitly exceptional lexical attribution; its relationship to the main root sense is uncertain.

cautions: The Lane material is retrieved under the contracted root عض, while the canonical QAC root is عضض; the public Quranic form is therefore normalized independently as عَضَّ.
Several rare botanical, anatomical, dialectal, and attributed meanings are retained as Classical Arabic evidence and are not being asserted as Quranic senses.
The two supplied Quran occurrences use the conventional body-part construction of biting in anger or regret; no modern Quran location has been inferred from Lane’s historical citation notation.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The exceptional meaning عُضَّاضٌ “tip of the nose” is reported by Maqayis as possibly deviating from the main root; it is retained separately with an explicit uncertainty condition.
